capabilities: Sync notes in real time across devices over direct WebRTC peer-to-peer channels
Pair devices by scanning a QR code with a single-use ECDH key exchange
Encrypt note content and obfuscate file paths locally with AES-256-GCM and HMAC
Reconcile offline divergent edits with a character-level three-way merge engine
Relay large binary attachments via the Blossom protocol addressed by SHA-256 hash
extras: Explicitly warns it is not a backup: relay mailboxes expire after about 7 days and R2 blobs after 10 days, so pair it with a backup solution. Not yet in the official community plugin directory, so it must be installed manually from the Releases page. Free; no accounts or paid services required when using public Nostr relays.
intentEvidence: Every common Obsidian sync alternative today forces you into an unwanted compromise
motivation: The author built it because existing sync alternatives "force you into an unwanted compromise" of subscriptions, third-party trust, or self-hosting complexity.
problem: Obsidian's sync options force a compromise: paid subscriptions, third-party cloud accounts, or complex self-hosted server stacks.

relations.evidence: Every common Obsidian sync alternative today forces you into an unwanted compromise

summary: Peer-to-peer real-time vault sync with end-to-end encryption, QR device pairing, and no accounts, subscriptions, or central servers.
